messages:
miriam: Heads-up — proposal to gate exports of raw/span-level telemetry at the collector by exporter + customer consent. Want to avoid accidental PII leakage to third-party exporters. Thoughts?

alex.k: +1. Is this gating at the config level (collector) or at ingest (service side)?

miriam: At collector level ideally. We can enforce per-exporter allowlists and per-customer consent flags. That keeps ingestion simple and centralizes policy.

tony: OK but two concerns: (1) How do we audit who requested/approved a decryption/export, (2) How to handle lawful-e2e for enterprise customers that need raw spans for debugging?

sara: For (1) we should create an "export-access" audit event that records: requester, org, exporter, reason, TTL, approver. Store in an immutable audit index for 7 years (or tenant-configurable). For (2) we can allow temporary scoped keys + workspace approval workflow.

miriam: Exactly what I had in mind. Proposed UX: in Console -> Telemetry -> Exporters, a toggle per-exporter that is "raw span export (PII risk)". Enabling opens a modal: select org scope, attach compliance ticket (Jira ID), choose TTL, and pick key policy. That action creates an approval workflow and an audit entry.

alex.k: From an implementation POV, collector config snippet could look like:

```yaml
export_policies:
  - exporter: honeycomb-prod
    require_approval: true
    allowed_orgs: [org-123, org-456]
    sampling_override: 0.01
    redact_attributes: [email, ssn, card_number]
    transform: pseudonymize

  - exporter: internal-blob
    require_approval: false
    allowed_orgs: [internal]
    retention_days: 365
```

alex.k: We also need runtime guards so an attacker who flips a flag can't silently start exporting. The collector should validate approvals against an external policy service and refuse to stream until the approval token is presented.

miriam: Yes — approval token + signed statement from KMS. Approval token is short-lived and includes an aud claim (exporter/org). Collector calls Policy API to verify the token before opening the exporter stream.

tony: About decryption: we can't just ship decrypted raw span payloads to external exporters. For exporters that must receive plaintext (some debugging partners), require a per-exporter KMS wrap where customer holds key material or we use customer-managed key (CMK) with explicit cross-account grants. Log every KMS decrypt/grant action.

sara: Agree. Audit requirements: each decrypt or grant should emit structured audit line with: action, key_id, grantee, request_ts, approver, justification. Index into our compliance-audit store.

telemetry-bot: Policy change detected: telemetry-export-gating v1 will add fields require_approval, approval_ttl, audit_stream. CI target: collector and policy-service.

miriam: Also proposal for quota-driven sampling: if a tenant doesn't have approved exporter, we sample more aggressively on spans containing sensitive attrs. That avoids data loss for metrics but prevents full-span leaks.

alex.k: How do we detect "sensitive attrs" reliably? We need a light-weight detector in the collector based on attribute names + regex checks, with a denylist that can be extended via remote config. Detector should be opt-in per workspace.

sara: We'll ship a default denylist (email, phone, ssn, card_num, bearer_token) and allow customers to add patterns. All detections generate anonymized evidence blobs (hashed) for audit without exposing raw value.

tony: Rollout plan: feature flag telemetry-redaction-v2. Start with internal orgs + a few pilot customers. Collector will run in canary mode — it emits both pre/post policy metrics for validation but only enforces for flagged orgs.

deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled: collector-3.7.0 -> canary cluster telemetry-canary-2 at 2026-03-21T02:00Z.

miriam: UX follow-ups: add a "pending approvals" view in Console and exportable CSV of audit events for compliance, plus webhook to send approval events to the customer's SIEM. Also need RBAC: only workspace admins + security roles can request enablement.

alex.k: One more: exporters that we don't control (3rd-party SaaS) should be restricted to pseudonymized payloads by default; we can provide a partner SDK that can accept hashed identifiers and later re-identify if partner proves compliance via contract and KMS exchange.

sara: I'll draft the audit schema and event names (export_request.created, export_request.approved, kms.decrypt.granted, exporter.stream.opened, exporter.stream.closed) and put in the compliance doc.

miriam: Great — please comment in the PR I'll open (collector: feature/telemetry-export-gating). If no objections, plan to start pilot next week. :thumbsup:

tony: No objections from me. +1 to pilot.

alex.k: +1. Will add tests to ensure token verification and audit emission.

sara: +1. Will coordinate with legal on contract language for partner exports.

miriam: Thanks everyone — filing the PR now and tagging @product-security for review.
